accuracy.evidence: All values for B(12, 0.3) recomputed independently in Python with math.comb and in the lab's own BCUMART.cdf: P(X ≤ 0) = 0.0138, P(X ≤ 1) = 0.0850, P(X ≤ 2) = 0.2528, P(X ≤ 3) = 0.4925, P(X ≤ 5) = 0.8822, P(X ≤ 7) = 0.9905; P(X ≥ 4) = 0.5075, P(X > 5) = 0.1178, P(3 ≤ X ≤ 7) = 0.7377, P(2 < X < 6) = 0.6293, P(4 ≤ X < 9) = 0.5058. p-drag: P(X ≤ 2) = 0.1513 at p = 0.35 and 0.0834 at p = 0.40, so 0.40 is the first 0.05 step under 0.1; P(X ≤ 3) at p = 0.5 is 0.0730. Identities P(X ≥ k) = 1 − P(X ≤ k − 1) and P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = P(X ≤ b) − P(X ≤ a − 1) as in the A level content and standard texts.

misconceptions.evidence: Every documented boundary slip in examiner reports on binomial cumulative questions is targeted: 1 − P(X ≤ k) for 'at least k' (step 1 predict, the k + 1 bar slip, tags tail7, m6, p1), 'fewer than' read as ≤ (step 0 predict '0 to 6', off-by-one set feedback, tags incl9/short, m8, p2), subtracting P(X ≤ a) for a range (range slips, tags drop5/extra, p4, p5, m2), picking the wrong tail (tags wrongside, flip, context tiles), complement arithmetic (same/over, m1, m7), and misjudging how p moves the distribution (step 3 predict, tags rises/same3, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 356 flagbinp builds the nCr p^r (1 − p)^(n − r) formula and shades a pmf; flagcumfreq is about grouped-data cumulative frequency. This lab works on the cumulative distribution function itself: the learner selects whole-number value sets from inequality words on a number line, taps the cdf bar to subtract for tails, taps top and bottom cdf bars for ranges, and drags p to move a lower tail below a threshold.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the boundary rule by doing it: the Check button refuses a set that keeps 6 for 'fewer than 6' and names the slip; tapping the bar k + 1 for an upper tail is refused with the reason, and the correct tap shows 1 − 0.4925 = 0.5075 worked out; ranges require choosing the top bar and the bar just below the range, with the subtraction shown. Dragging p shows the whole distribution sliding and the shaded tail shrinking. Context tiles transfer the rule to words.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: '0 to 6' for fewer than 6 (the set check rejects 6), 'P(X ≤ 4)' for P(X ≥ 4) = 1 − ? (the bar-4 tap is refused with the reason), and 'goes up' for P(X ≤ 3) as p rises (the drag shows the tail shrinking). A.reveal reports each prediction in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, every wrong option tagged with feedback naming the slip: tail7/wrongside, incl9/short, drop5/extra, same/over (complement of 0.4925), rises/same3 (effect of p, with 0.0730), strict/flip. In the lab, off-by-one sets, wrong tail bars, wrong top or bottom bars and each wrong context tile get their own message.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid 3.2 (limit 6.5) and adult 8.4 (limit 9.5). Notation is introduced with one worked number each (P(X ≤ 3) = 0.4925, P(X ≥ 4) = 0.5075, P(3 ≤ X ≤ 7) = P(X ≤ 7) − P(X ≤ 2)). The A level terms cumulative distribution function, complement, upper and lower tail, strict and inclusive inequality are named in the adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to every lesson, including 356 binomial probabilities. Each kid paragraph does one job: translate words to values, what P(X ≤ k) is, upper tails, ranges. The adult text gives the specification fit, the key terms with the lab's values, and the boundary mistakes with a checking habit.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and desktop screenshots of every step after Show me (.tmp_run/shots/bc-*). The 13 value dots and 13 bars fit across 390 px with 11–12 px labels and full-height tap columns about 24 px wide; every bar also has a P(X ≤ k) button; the p handle is 32 × 38 px on a 54 px tall hit band; context tiles are full width and 52 px tall; feedback with worked subtraction wraps inside the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every tap or drag has a button (Check, Clear, Keep next value, P(X ≤ 0) … P(X ≤ 8), p − 0.05 / p + 0.05, each expression). The canvas aria-label reads the phrase and kept values, the cumulative values, the range phase, p with the tail value, or the situation and options after every action; messages are spoken with c.say.
